title: Brand Templates Your Team Can Reuse: How to Keep Your Brand Consistent Without a Designer on Call

cards.heading: Start with what you make most
cards.text: Slides, quotes, social posts. If the request has come up three times, it needs a template.

cards.heading: Build in software your team uses
cards.text: A template nobody can edit comfortably will be ignored. Test it on another computer.

cards.heading: Lock the logo, colours and fonts
cards.text: Leave words and images open. Locking prevents accidents, not determined changes.

cards.heading: Hand over editable files
cards.text: A PDF is not a template. Add a one-page guide and confirm what you own in writing.

cards.heading: Name one owner
cards.text: One master copy and one person responsible stop old versions spreading.

facebook.message:
Does every slide deck in your business look slightly different?
Most people do not read brand guidelines before building a slide. They open the last file and change it. Good templates make the on-brand option the quick one. Our latest guide covers which templates are worth having, what to lock, and how to hand them over. Swipe through for the key points.

To read the full article, visit the FinTaxTech website and find "Brand Templates Your Team Can Reuse: How to Keep Your Brand Consistent Without a Designer on Call" in our Blog section.
